newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Selective blue chips lift Manila shares at close.
newsitem.headline: Selective blue chips lift Manila shares at close.

text.p: * But value turnover remains slim at 2.58 bln pesos
A slight technical rally in selected blue chips in late session on Thursday saw the Manila share index snapping out of a seven-day losing streak, traders said.
"The market's been down for several days and so there's this technical rally but it's unlikely to be sustained for long," said Henry Ong, senior analyst at Sapphire Securities.
Main index ended up 6.06 points or 0.19 percent to 3,206.67.

"Overall, the market is still weak as there's not much volume and we are still hovering in that 3,200 support,' said Rudsend Alpay, assistant vice-president at Lippo Securities. He added that end-of-the-month liquidation by investors may add pressure on the main index in the coming sessions.
Some 8.7 billion shares changed hands valued at 2.58 billion pesos compared with daily value turnover ranging from three to four billion pesos.
PLDT, which was in negative territory for most of the session, perked up in late session to lead blue chips including Meralco B and San Miguel Corp B higher.
Second and thirdliners also manifested strength. Among the gainers and most actively traded stocks were Lepanto Consolidated Mining Co and Polar Mines & Development Corp.
All sectors rose except for the property sector. Gainers outnumbered losers 70 to 46 with 85 issues unchanged.
Sapphire's Ong said that although the market may sustain today's slight upsurge on Friday, the rally may be limited because of the long Lenten holiday next week.
